name: Naomi
bio:
Naomi is the mother-in-law of Ruth and the emotional center of the book that bears her daughter-in-law's name. She and her husband Elimelech leave Bethlehem for Moab to escape a famine, taking their two sons Mahlon and Chilion. In Moab, Elimelech dies, and years later both sons die as well, leaving Naomi without husband or children in a foreign land. When she hears that the LORD has again given Israel bread, she decides to return to Bethlehem and urges her two Moabite daughters-in-law, Orpah and Ruth, to go back to their own families instead of following her into an uncertain future. Orpah turns back, but Ruth clings to her.

Naomi arrives home and tells the women of Bethlehem to call her "Mara" ("bitter") instead of Naomi ("pleasant"), saying the LORD has dealt bitterly with her and brought her home empty. Yet she is not passive in her grief: she recognizes Boaz as a close relative with power to redeem their family's land and name, and she coaches Ruth, step by step, toward seeking his protection at the threshing floor. When Boaz marries Ruth and they have a son, the women of Bethlehem tell Naomi that this child will renew her life and sustain her in old age — and Naomi, once empty, becomes the one who holds and nurses her grandson Obed, the grandfather of King David. Her story moves from bitterness and emptiness to quiet restoration through loyalty and God's providence working through ordinary faithfulness.
